prompt: Review application security for an import service where untrusted URLs, archives, output paths, and converter options reach network, filesystem, parser, subprocess, and logging sinks. Define safe invariants and failure paths.

Fix input validation for a JSON API with nested filters and attachments: use typed schemas and explicit limits, then ensure later decoding/canonicalization cannot change an accepted value into a dangerous path or query.

Design session security for the native client, including protected token storage, restart restoration, expiry/renewal/revocation, sensitive-action reauthentication, and secret-safe logs/crash artifacts.

Assess the application attack surface where stored database values later become webhook URLs, file names, templates, and process arguments. Trace each source to its privileged sink and remove unsafe reinterpretation.
Harden the upload/extract/convert pipeline with path containment, archive/decompression limits, safe process arguments, bounded parsing, deterministic cleanup, and non-sensitive errors/logging.

Perform a broad security review and produce findings with exploit prerequisites, severity rationale, false-positive self-checks, and remediation verification across application, cloud, dependency, and identity surfaces.
Define tenant, object, field, relationship, and action permissions for each user role, including delegation and revocation; parsing and sink safety are already complete.
Design passkey/password/MFA login, enrollment, phishing resistance, throttling, recovery, authenticator replacement, and fresh-authentication policy; wider application data flows are out of scope.
Review the browser client for XSS, CSRF, CSP, CORS, clickjacking, cookie flags, URL/origin handling, and postMessage validation; backend/non-browser sinks are not part of the assignment.
Design confinement for an untrusted scripting runtime with memory/type safety, host-call capabilities, fuel limits, module loading restrictions, and sandbox-escape tests.

The security review has identified suspicious data flows; use application security to trace inputs through parsing/files/network/process/log sinks and define exact controls, while the parent review retains severity and finding ownership.

The feature needs both an authorization review and application security. Keep entitlement policy in authorization-security while application-security owns schema parsing, canonical paths, outbound destinations, serialization, process arguments, and failure cleanup.

Harden input validation and privileged IPC for an Electron app. Desktop engineering owns process/window integration; application-security owns trust boundaries, message schemas, limits, canonical file paths, external URLs, and privileged sink rules.
A historical security report describes malformed imports. The actual request is only to update its table of contents; do not assess or change runtime behavior.
An old permission bug includes malformed identifier examples. Extract the issue date and owner only; no current parser or policy work is requested.
A desktop README mentions checking IPC payloads. Rename a documentation heading only and leave all validation and runtime code unchanged.
